title: Cotton fabric
content: Cotton is easy to sew and suitable for tote bags, pouches, scrunchies, and small accessories.

title: Denim fabric
content: Denim is durable and suitable for sturdy pouches, bags, coasters, and patchwork products.

title: Silk fabric
content: Silk is lightweight and slippery. Use an appropriate needle and handle it carefully while sewing.

title: Tote bag
content: A tote bag can be made from sturdy cotton, canvas, or denim. Check that the fabric fits all required pattern pieces.

title: Zipper pouch
content: A zipper pouch usually needs two fabric panels, a zipper, and optional lining. Check the dimensions before cutting.

title: Scrunchie
content: A scrunchie needs a fabric strip and elastic. The required fabric dimensions depend on the desired size.

title: Seam allowance
content: Allow extra fabric for seams when required by the pattern. Check whether the listed dimensions already include seam allowance.

title: Measure fabric
content: Measure the usable length and width of each scrap, excluding damaged or unusable sections.

title: Reuse small scraps
content: Small fabric scraps can be reused for patchwork, appliqué, bookmarks, and other craft projects.

title: Match fabric to products
content: Compare each scrap's dimensions with every required pattern piece before recommending a product.

title: Linen fabric
content: Linen is breathable and suitable for reusable bags, simple pouches, and decorative fabric products.

title: Thick fabric
content: Thick fabric can be useful for sturdy bags and organizers. Check whether the sewing machine and needle can handle its thickness.

title: Stretch fabric
content: Stretch fabric may need a stretch stitch and a suitable needle to help seams move without breaking.

title: Fabric condition
content: Inspect scraps before reuse. Avoid fabric with mold, contamination, or extensive damage, and clean and dry suitable scraps before storing them.

title: Check fabric dimensions
content: Measure both the length and width of the usable fabric area. A scrap must fit the required pattern piece in both dimensions.

title: Account for seam allowance
content: Check whether a pattern's measurements include seam allowance. Add the required allowance before cutting if it is not included.

title: Match multiple scraps
content: Several small scraps may work together for patchwork, but each individual pattern piece must fit a suitable piece of fabric.

title: Check fabric quantity
content: Compare the available quantity of each scrap with the number of pieces required by the selected product pattern.

title: Prevent fraying
content: Woven fabric edges may fray after cutting. Consider zigzag stitching, an overlocker, or another suitable edge finish.

title: Choose a suitable needle
content: Choose a sewing needle suited to the fabric type and thickness. Test the needle and stitch settings on a spare piece first.

title: Prepare fabric before cutting
content: Remove loose threads, inspect damaged sections, and press fabric flat before measuring and cutting pattern pieces.

title: Make patchwork products
content: Small fabric scraps can be joined into a larger patchwork panel for products such as pouches, bags, and decorative items.

title: Reduce cutting waste
content: Arrange pattern pieces carefully before cutting and save usable leftover sections for smaller sewing projects.

title: Share unused fabric
content: If a fabric scrap is not useful for your current project, consider sharing or exchanging it with someone who can reuse it.

title: Find missing fabric
content: If available scraps are insufficient for a product, identify the missing fabric dimensions and search for compatible scraps from other users.
